summary: Lane bursts: `fractal agents burst AGENT --cores N --memory SIZE --reason TEXT --as AGENT` raises a laned seat's lane for one command's run and gives it back when the command's holder ends, waiting in order for room as a step's raise does; scripts/fractal-test asks for one sized by .st/lane-bursts.json before it takes a pool tree and records burst and burst_wait_s, and the daily report shows lane waits as their own line

replay.detail: No claim kind and no graph change: bursts live in the daemon's memory.

schema.detail: No schema change. A run's runs.jsonl line gains burst, burst_wait_s and, when it held none, burst_none; scripts/fractal-test-report gains waits.

rules.detail: A laned seat's live lane is the largest of its own lane, each step it holds and its burst. A burst that does not fit waits (reason `burst lane …`) in the order bursts asked; one that can never fit is refused. A lapsed lease drops the burst and is counted in doctor --performance. A change to a running laned seat's declared capacity resizes its live lane, as the code already did; the design note now says so.

compatibility.detail: New route POST/DELETE /v1/agents/lane/burst (agent and actor in the body) and CLI command `agents burst`, whose --as takes only an agent. An older daemon answers 404 and the holder prints `none`; an older fractal has no `agents burst`, and scripts/fractal-test then holds no burst, says so, and runs the checks in the lane as it is. A seat without a lane or a host with lanes off holds none. While its daemon cannot be reached, the holder waits for it (within the run's --queue-limit) rather than answering.

manual.detail: No manual step. Builder seats get base lanes only once this is on main and rolled to their host.

recovery.detail: Revert. A burst held when the daemon rolls back stays on the slice until the lane's next lowering or the seat's next start.
